title: How Chords Are Built
description: Stack two 3rds and you've got a chord. Which 3rds you pick decides how it sounds.

steps.title: Stacking 3rds
steps.description:
A triad is three notes stacked in 3rds. A 3rd comes in two sizes: a major 3rd is 4 semitones (4 keys up, counting black ones), and a minor 3rd is 3. Mix and match them and you get four kinds of chord:

• Major: 4 + 3
• Minor: 3 + 4
• Diminished: 3 + 3
• Augmented: 4 + 4

steps.title: C major (4 + 3)
steps.description: From C, count up 4 keys to E. From E, count up 3 more to G. Play C, E and G together.
steps.hint: C, E, G. Three white keys, skipping one each time.

steps.title: C minor (3 + 4)
steps.description: Now flip it. From C count up just 3 keys to Eb, then 4 more to G. Only the middle note moved, but listen to how much darker it gets.
steps.hint: Take your C major chord and drop the E to the black key just below it.

steps.title: B diminished (3 + 3)
steps.description: Two small 3rds stacked: B up 3 to D, D up 3 to F. It sounds squeezed and uneasy, like it's waiting for something to happen.
steps.hint: B, D, F. All white keys, starting on the B just below C5.

steps.title: C augmented (4 + 4)
steps.description: Two big 3rds stacked: C up 4 to E, E up 4 to G#. It floats and doesn't quite settle. Think dream sequence in an old film.
steps.hint: Play C major, then push the G up one key to G#.

steps.title: An easy way to remember
steps.description:
Think of the two 3rds as big (4) and small (3):

• Major: big, then small. Bright.
• Minor: small, then big. Darker.
• Diminished: small, small. Tense.
• Augmented: big, big. Unsettled.

You can also check the outer notes. Root to top is 7 semitones for both major and minor, 6 for diminished and 8 for augmented.
